hyps.why: Above ~0.08 Adam steps overshoot and diverge, so further increases hurt much more than elsewhere.
With learning rates of 1e-5 to 1.3e-4 the network is under-trained after 243 epochs, so raising the rate helps most there.
Tiny batches give noisy gradients, so larger steps destabilise training more.
At low learning rates, fewer updates per epoch make under-training worse.
At high learning rates, larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilise aggressive steps.
At alpha 0.13 to 1 the L2 penalty dominates, so increasing it further causes severe under-fitting.
Lowering a diverging learning rate brings it back into the stable regime.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to instability and dead units under large steps.
Wider layers are more sensitive to large learning rates and are more likely to diverge.
At low learning rates, smaller batches give more updates and reduce under-training.
